definition: Predicting several continuous targets jointly, exploiting correlations between outputs.
details: Predicting several continuous targets jointly, exploiting correlations between outputs.

explainer.lead: Multi-target regression predicts several continuous targets jointly rather than one at a time. It matters because exploiting correlations between outputs can improve predictions.

tiers.eli5: Instead of guessing each measurement separately, you predict someone's height and weight together, since they tend to move together.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers model correlated outputs jointly to share signal across targets. A pitfall is that target correlations can help or hurt, so joint modeling is not automatically better.
tiers.paperLevel: The model maps inputs to several continuous targets simultaneously, exploiting correlations between outputs.

explainer.example: Predicting a house's price and rental yield together in one model rather than with two separate regressors.
